Biventricular size and qualitative systolic function were normal in both twins, as was conotruncal anatomy and aortic and ductal arch anatomy.

in_text_mentions: le neonate born via normal vaginal delivery on January 2, 2024, at 10 pm in a tertiary care hospital in central India. The infant, initially unresponsive and not crying at birth, was promptly transferred to the neonatal intensive care unit (NICU) due to respiratory distress. Syndromic features were noted, including a depressed nasal bridge, small dysplastic ears, upward slanting of the eyes, a single transverse palmar crease, flat face, poor moro reflex, hypotonia, short neck, and joint hyperflexibility, leading to a clinical diagnosis of Down syndrome confirmed through karyotyping (Figure 1).
